items.issue: commodityHeading(code) builds /^(.+ \()?CODE\)?$/, which accepts any commodity name or none, and unbalanced brackets ('0102)', 'Cow (0102'). The frontend renders an exact heading (namedLegendFor: 'Cow (0102)' when the commodity has a name, else the bare code), yet commodities.spec.ts:63 asserts toHaveAccessibleName(commodityHeading(code)): if the page dropped or misspelt the commodity name, or showed the wrong one, that assertion stays green. The repo already holds the expected names in domain/animals/constants/commodity-names.ts ('0102': 'Cow').
items.fix: Must: the heading assertion names the exact heading the page should show for each code, so a missing or wrong commodity name turns it red. One way: build the expected string from commodityNames ('${commodityNames[code]} (${code})', or the bare code when there is no name) and assert with toHaveAccessibleName(string); keep a loose pattern only for the commodityGroups locator.

items.issue: commodityHeading(code) (line 61) returns a RegExp for a checkbox group's accessible name, not a heading: its value word mispredicts what it returns. Its parameter 'code' is also handed a regex fragment, not a code, at line 70 (commodityHeading('\\d+')). And AnimalIdentificationPage.commodityHeading(heading) in page-objects/animals/animal-identification-page.ts:61 returns a Locator under the same name, so one name means two different things in sibling page objects.
items.fix: Must: the method's name says it returns a pattern for a commodity group's name, its parameter holds what callers pass, and it no longer shares a name with a Locator-returning method on a sibling page object. One way: rename to commodityGroupNamePattern(codePattern: string) and update commodityGroup, commodityGroups and commodities.spec.ts:63.

items.issue: commodityHeading(code) returns a RegExp, not a heading: in this file boldMatchInCommodityHeading and selectedCommodityHeading return Locators, and AnimalIdentificationPage.commodityHeading (animal-identification-page.ts:61) is a Locator too, so one name returns two kinds of value across sibling page objects. Its parameter 'code' is also handed a regex fragment, not a code: commodityGroups (line 70) calls commodityHeading('\\d+'), and the value is interpolated into the RegExp unescaped.
items.fix: Must: the name of the member that builds the group's accessible-name matcher says it returns a name pattern (not a heading locator), and its parameter holds what callers pass. One way: rename to commodityGroupName(code) returning the exact expected name (see the companion finding), and give commodityGroups its own literal pattern rather than passing '\\d+' as a code.

items.issue: The pattern ^(.+ \()?CODE\)?$ at line 62 accepts either a bare code or 'Name (code)', with the two brackets optional independently, so it also matches 'Live bovine (0102' and '0102)'. commodities.spec.ts:63 asserts toHaveAccessibleName(commodityHeading(code)) through it, so that test passes whether a result group's legend is the named form the frontend builds (namedLegendFor -> 'Name (code)', pinned as 'Cow (0102)' in the frontend's labels.test.js:7) or a fallback to the bare code: deleting the name from namedLegendFor turns no ins-tests assertion red.
items.fix: Must: the group-legend assertion pins the exact legend each group shows, so the test fails if a named group's legend loses its name, and the pattern never matches a half-bracketed name. One way: keep the expected names of the commodity codes the specs use in a domain constant copied from the frontend's commodity names, build the exact legend ('Name (code)' or the code alone) from it, and use getByRole('group', { name, exact: true }); if a pattern must stay for the commodityGroups count, write it as ^(?:.+ \(\d+\)|\d+)$.

items.issue: Title 'leaves a species of more than one animal unsaved when Save and continue is pressed' names the wrong button: the test clicks saveAndReturnToOverview ('Save and return to overview', base-page.ts:293) at line 101, and also asserts the return to the overview (line 102), which the title does not state
items.fix: Must: the title names the button the test presses and states what its assertions prove. One way: 'leaves a species of more than one animal unsaved when Save and return to overview is pressed'

items.issue: The heading assertion was loosened, not updated. commodities.spec.ts:63 now checks each group against commodityHeading(code), the regex ^(.+ \()?<code>\)?$ (commodity-selection-page.ts:61-63). It passes for the old bare-code legend ('0102'), for any name at all ('Anything (0102)'), and for unbalanced text ('0102)', 'Cow (0102'). The frontend now heads groups 'Cow (0102)' via namedLegendFor (commodity-legend.js:5-8), so reverting that change leaves this test green, and the title's claim 'lists ... groups by commodity heading' is proven only for the code part.
items.fix: Must: the test fails if a commodity group's heading is not exactly the heading the page is meant to show, the name and code in brackets for a named commodity and the code alone for an unnamed one. One way: add a test-data map of expected headings for the codes GROUPING_QUERIES returns (for example 0102 -> 'Cow (0102)', 01061900 -> '01061900') and assert toHaveAccessibleName(expectedHeading, exact); keep the regex only for locating groups, or have commodityGroup take the exact heading.

items.issue: commodityHeading(code), called at commodities.spec.ts:63 and defined at commodity-selection-page.ts:61-63, does not return a heading. It returns a RegExp that matches any heading ending in the code. Its parameter 'code' also takes a regex fragment: commodityGroups passes '\\d+' (commodity-selection-page.ts:70), and a real code is put into the pattern without escaping. A reader of line 63 would expect an exact heading string.
items.fix: Must: the page-object member the spec calls says it returns a pattern for matching headings, and its parameter says whether it takes a commodity code or a regex fragment. One way: rename it commodityHeadingPattern and split it so commodityGroups builds its own any-code pattern, or remove it if the first finding's exact expected headings replace it.

items.issue: Title 'lists reference-data's groups by commodity heading and each group's species by label, in that order' is untrue: the test and REQ-015 order groups by code, and the heading now reads 'Name (code)'. Linked 5 times from workspace coverage.json.
items.fix: Must: the title states the order tested. One way: '...groups by commodity code and each group's species by label...', renaming the coverage links in step.

items.issue: One rule, 6 findings: #1, #2, #3, #4, #6, #7 — commodityHeading(code) is a loose regex that accepts any name, none, or unbalanced brackets, so the heading check cannot fail; and its name says heading but returns a RegExp fed regex fragments. Two reviewers raised each point.
items.fix: Must: one page-object member owns the expected group name per code, asserted exactly; its name says what it returns. One way: commodityGroupName(code) built from domain/animals/constants/commodity-names.ts ('Cow (0102)' or the bare code), asserted with toHaveAccessibleName exact; commodityGroups keeps its own literal pattern.
